# Scheduled compliance polling and alerting — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Atlas billing alerts can operate at organization or project scope, but conditions differ: yesterday’s billed-amount threshold supports both scopes; the organization’s monthly-total and any-single-project monthly-total conditions are organization alerts. Monthly-total alerts reset when the pending invoice closes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions/ · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting
- [statement] MongoDB warns that simultaneous daily subscription uplift and unmet-minimum charges at the paying organization’s billing-period end can trigger daily maximum billing alerts. A commitment-compliance review should examine these charges before treating the alert as an operational usage spike. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/ · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For a tagging-compliance rule, the FinOps Foundation playbook compares the cost of policy-compliant resources with total cloud cost and permits a taggable-resource denominator to exclude resources that cannot be tagged. It identifies tagging requirements and responsible roles; an identified organizational tagging compliance target is optional. (low confidence) — https://www.finops.org/wg/how-to-measure-tagging-policy-compliance/ · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting
- [statement] The mongodb/atlas-billing repository documents daily billing imports and separately scheduled processing, providing historical implementation evidence for periodic Atlas billing collection. Its README explicitly marks the solution deprecated and unmaintained, so it is not a current supported polling recommendation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/atlas-billing · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Scheduled FinOps compliance checks evaluate deployed resources against explicit policies, retain findings for historical review, and notify responsible teams. Combining Google’s scheduled-evaluation example with the FinOps Foundation’s tagging-compliance playbook suggests checking required metadata and routing violations to an accountable owner; this is a design inference, not evidence of a native Atlas compliance-polling service. (medium confidence) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/cost-management/automate-financial-governance-policies-using-workload-manager · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting · also: https://www.finops.org/wg/how-to-measure-tagging-policy-compliance/
- [statement] Google’s November 4, 2025 Workload Manager example supports scheduled evaluations from hourly to monthly, custom OPA Rego policies, export of findings to BigQuery, and notifications through channels including email, Slack and PagerDuty. This demonstrates a Google Cloud implementation pattern; it does not establish direct coverage of Atlas organizations or commitment contracts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-04) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/cost-management/automate-financial-governance-policies-using-workload-manager · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting
- [statement] Atlas’s yesterday-billed-amount alert ignores credits applied for that day. Its documented daily and monthly billing conditions therefore should not be assumed to represent real-time net spending or enforce a spending cap; the documentation describes threshold notifications. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions/ · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/
- [statement] A 2024 Cloud Custodian discussion reports different underutilized-resource counts for local and periodic execution of an EC2 policy with a 30-day window and period: 3600. The accepted response recommends removing that explicit period, and the reporter confirmed success. This historical case supports validating scheduled results against a known baseline; it does not prove a current unfixed defect or an Atlas defect. (low confidence) — https://github.com/orgs/cloud-custodian/discussions/9401 · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting
- [statement] The ABACUS paper’s abstract explicitly distinguishes alerting teams after budget thresholds are breached from blocking new deployments to enforce budgets. These are separate mechanisms; notifications alone do not establish preventive enforcement. The abstract provides no evidence of Atlas integration. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14753 · keywords: Scheduled compliance polling and alerting
